tasks.gr11-layered-rocks-karoo-t2: Topic: Layered Rocks and Karoo Landscapes. Cover sedimentary rock formation (deposition, compaction, cementation), the Karoo Supergroup, horizontal and tilted strata, cuestas, hogbacks, and how these features appear on topographic maps. Ask Grade 11 learners to distinguish between a cuesta and a hogback, explain how the Karoo Basin formed, or interpret a geological cross-section.
tasks.gr11-igneous-landforms-t2: Topic: Massive Igneous Landforms. Cover intrusive vs extrusive igneous rocks, the types of intrusive bodies (dykes, sills, laccoliths, batholiths), the formation of dolerite domes and koppies in the Karoo, inselbergs/bornhardts, and examples from South Africa (Cape Granite Suite, Pilanesberg). Ask Grade 11 learners to explain the difference between a dyke and a sill, describe how a koppie forms, or identify igneous features on a topographic map.
tasks.gr11-slopes-mass-movement-t2: Topic: Slopes and Mass Movement. Cover slope components (crest, free face, debris slope, pediment), factors affecting slope stability (rock type, climate, vegetation, human activity), types of mass movement (rockfall, landslide, mudflow, soil creep, solifluction), and prevention measures. Ask Grade 11 learners to classify a mass movement event, explain how deforestation increases slope instability, or describe slope profile components.
tasks.gr11-geomorphology-mapwork-t2: Topic: Geomorphology and Topographic Mapwork. Cover how to identify geological and geomorphological features on South African 1:50 000 topographic maps, constructing and interpreting cross-sections, identifying slope types (concave, convex, uniform), and linking contour patterns to rock type and structure. Ask Grade 11 learners to draw a topographic cross-section, identify landforms from contour patterns, or calculate a gradient between two points.
tasks.gr11-fieldwork-weather-data-t2: Topic: Fieldwork and weather data (Grade 11 Geography, Term 2). Cover weather instruments (thermometer in a Stevenson screen, rain gauge, anemometer, wind vane, barometer), recording and processing data (total, mean, range), choosing graphs (line, bar, map, synoptic chart). Give all data in the question.
